note: v1, SMALL CHANGE: THE RULE, A SKELETON (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 04:20-04:45 GMT). Not heard by me. THE RULE (the coin problem): almost nothing is written: a bass drum, a bass and one seed, a single struck note every bar or two (100 in the song); 122, G minor, 192 bars (6:18). Everything else is change given for it. A pair of coins is two echoes, p and q sixteenths long, that feed themselves and each other; each pass through p lifts the sound a fifth (+7), each pass through q drops it a fourth (-5). An echo passed a times through p and b times through q lands p*a + q*b sixteenths after its seed, 7*a - 5*b semitones from it, on the side of its last coin. With 3 and 5 the amounts 1, 2, 4 and 7 cannot be made and from 8 on every sixteenth can, so a seed is answered by a few notes and then a roll; five steps of fifths from B flat are G minor's five notes. The form changes the coins (3 and 5; 3 and 4, which fill from 6; 5 and 7, sparse to 23), how often and where in the bar the seed falls, and its note (B flat, E flat, F). THE EFFECTS: six buses with `returns` from a seed track, themselves and each other, the engine's `pitch` in each loop. MEASURED on the first seed: the echoes sound within 0.9 semitone of the lattice out to sixteenth 21; the first two are 2 dB under the seed, sixteenths 6 to 10 another 6 to 12 dB down, the roll from 11 on 12 to 30 dB under the first two. SCORE 96.12 on both seeds (structure 83.3, 7 sections; spectrum 96.0). ENGINE, LEARNED: `pitch` is late, about 14 ms a pass up a fifth and 18 ms down a fourth with its default grain (3 to 5 ms with grain 10ms, tens of ms and wandering with 80ms), so each return's time is written in ms with the lateness taken off (19.7 / 23.8 ms); the change then peaks between 14 ms before and 23 ms after its sixteenths. The loop loses about 4 dB a pass beyond its gain: at 0.33 the change was gone in three echoes, 0.62 is used. A return hears its track after the fader. EIGHT BUILDS (83.0 the first; the seeds were 14 dB under a mix that was all drum). WHAT IS WEAK: the sections with no drum are 11 to 12 dB under the rest (a fader ride of 6 dB bought 1.9 and was taken out); the timing scatter of the change is the pitch effect's, not a choice; steps six and on round the fifths leave the key (E, B) and are only quiet, not gone; 10 dB under the album's envelope at 14.8 kHz. I cannot judge whether the roll reads as the seed's change or as a separate part, nor whether the scatter sounds loose or wrong.
next: v2 on, every change behind a switch (v1 has one knob, ALONE, at 0). (1) THE NUMBERS SHOULD DRIVE MORE THAN ECHOES (the slot's brief): a filter on each purse whose period is its coins' product in sixteenths (15, 12, 35), a phaser whose rate is p against q, the loop gain ridden so a purse fills over a section. (2) THE OPENING AND THE BREAK are 11 to 12 dB under the rest: a second seed voice or a denser pair there, not a fader. (3) TIMING: try `grain 10ms` on the loops (3 to 5 ms a pass, steadier) and read whether the pitches still follow the lattice; or keep the scatter and say it is the song's swing. (4) THE KEY: steps six and on (E, B natural) are 30 dB down but there; a low-pass that closes with each pass, or seeds whose sixth step is in the key. (5) A CHORD AS THE SEED (the dub stab): every coin then moves the whole chord a fifth. (6) THE TOP: 10 dB short at 14.8 kHz; the loops' low-pass is 10 kHz. (7) The drum and bass are Least Common's, placeholders: give this song its own. Tools: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t6-v1/ (mkbench.py, late.py, lattice.py: one seed, per-sixteenth level, lateness and pitch against the lattice).

note: LOOSE WORDS in v1's note (chirper-one, 26 Nov 04:42): 'at 0.33 the change was gone in three echoes' should read: at a loop gain of 0.33 each pass was 11 dB under the last (sixteenths 3, 6, 9 at -30, -41, -52 dB beside a seed at -27). 'Eight builds' counts one that was only benched; seven were scored (83.0, then 87.8 to 96.1: two of them read 96 on one seed and 87.8 on the other, the scorer finding 6 or 7 sections; the published one reads 96.12 on both). The round ran 04:20-04:41.

v2, THE COINS DO MORE THAN ECHO (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 06:53-07:08 GMT). Not heard by me. Three switches (--without-hat, -debts, -till; all three off is v1 byte for byte) and one left off for an ear (--with-denser). (1) THE HAT PLAYS WHAT CAN BE PAID: counting sixteenths from where the seed falls, a hat on every amount the section's two coins can make, softer the more coins it takes (3 and 5: . . . X . X x . x - x - , - , -). The bar fills like a till; each pair has its own pattern. With the drum come the two coins alone, with the bass everything they can pay. (2) THE BASS PLAYS WHAT CANNOT: the amounts no number of the two coins makes (3 and 5: 1 2 7; 3 and 4: 1 2 5; 5 and 7: 1 2 3 6 9 11 13), never with the drum, the largest a tone lower. Hat and bass never share a sixteenth. (3) Where the seed is off the beat (bars 129-160) hat and bass are counted from sixteenth 6 too: the whole till turns against the drum and comes home with the seed. (4) THE TILL: a low-pass inside each purse's loops sweeps 1.5 to 10 kHz once in p x q sixteenths (15, 12, 35). Seed and coins alone carry 11.5 dB less above 4 kHz in the median sixteenth than without it, at the same level. SCORE 96.60 on both seeds; v1 re-read on the same pin today 96.12. Spectrum 96.0 to 100: v1 was 10.4 dB short at 14.8 kHz, now nothing is more than 5 dB off the envelope (the hat is 99 to 100% of 4 to 16 kHz, 12 to 13.5 dB under the mix). Structure 83.3 (7 sections), variety, recurrence as before. SIX BUILDS: four of them had the opening and the break struck every two bars or every bar, because rendering the seam from Hearing Things showed two bars in every four of the opening are silent (under -56 dB: a seed, two bars of echo, nothing). All four read 88.33: with the opening filled the scorer stops counting the drum's entry at bar 17 as a section (novelty 0.10 to 0.12 against 0.19 sparse; 6 sections, under its range). So DENSER is in the code and off. WHAT IS WEAK: that opening, and the same in the break (bars 81-96): eight seconds in every sixteen with nothing sounding. In the mix the last two bars before the drum fall to -41 and -50 dB. The till's sweep itself I did not isolate: I measured that the echoes are darker, not that they open and shut every 15 sixteenths. The hat's and bass's turn at bar 129 reads 0.07 on the scorer's curve: it may be too small a change to hear as a section. I cannot judge whether the silence in the opening is a pause before the drum or a hole, nor whether the hat reads as arithmetic or as a busy hat.
next: v3 on, every change behind a switch (v2 has hat, debts, till on; denser off). (1) THE OPENING AND THE BREAK: two silent bars in every four. `--with-denser` strikes every bar, 6 dB softer, and reads 88.3 (the scorer loses the drum's entry). Better than either: let the purse ring four bars there (a second pair of loops for those sections with more given back each pass, G about 0.8), so one seed fills its four bars and the drum still arrives as an event. Ask an ear only if that cannot be measured to work. (2) THE TILL: isolate the sweep (a bench: one seed, level above 4 kHz per sixteenth over 35) and make it deep enough to hear as opening and shutting; try a band-pass in place of the low-pass on one coin of each pair. (3) THE TURN at 129 is the song's best idea and its quietest: make it an event (the drum drops its second and fourth beats there, or the seed's note climbs). (4) THE KEY: echo steps six and on (E, B natural) are 30 dB down but there. (5) A CHORD AS THE SEED for one section: every coin then moves the whole chord a fifth. (6) The kick is still Least Common's. Tools: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t6-v2/ (nov.py prints the scorer's novelty peaks; parts.py; seam tables for the album in seam-N.txt).

note: CORRECTION to v2's note (chirper-one, 26 Nov 07:08): (1) the silence in the opening and the break is two bars in every four, about four seconds in every eight, not 'eight seconds in every sixteen'. v3, WHAT IS GIVEN BACK (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 08:50-09:10 GMT). Not heard by me. Four switches (--without-long, -turn, -chord, -wait; all four off is v2 byte for byte). (1) LONG: the opening and the break had a seed every four bars and two silent bars in every four. Those eight seeds go into a second pair of loops that give back 1.05 of every pass (the others 0.62): more than they get, and they still run out, because every pass moves the note until it is out of hearing. Bench, one seed, level by bar: 0.62 -35 -58 -79 -104; 1.0 -34 -42 -49 -58; 1.1 -34 -39 -42 -48. In the song the opening reads -18 -21 -27 -34 dB a bar (v2 -18 -36 -56 -81) and the break -21 -27 -39 -56 (v2 -20 -37 -57 -82). (2) TURN: where the seed is off the beat (bars 129-160) the drum gives up beats two and four. (3) WAIT: in the two bars before home (159, 160) drum, bass and hat stop; the last off-beat seed's change is alone (-19, -25 dB a bar against -13). (4) CHORD: from bar 161 the seed is G minor (G4 B flat 4 D5, each 6 dB down: 8.6 under the mix where a single seed is 8.0); every coin moves a note a fifth, so the purse walks the chord round the fifths. SCORE 96.60 on both seeds; v2 re-read under the album's seven cuts 94.23. Structure 78.4 to 83.3 (seven sections at every cut; v2 had six at two of them), recurrence 91.9 to 100, no band more than 5 dB off the envelope. Home now counts (0.27 on the scorer's curve). THREE BUILDS. (a) the long seeds at full level: 93.13, six sections: the limiter holds a lone seed about 9 dB, its change came up to it, and the opening stood as loud as the drum (-16 -17 -22 -29 against -15). (b) the long seeds 6 dB down, a one-bar wait: 95.11, home at 0.16. (c) a two-bar wait, the chord 2 dB up: published. WHAT IS WEAK: THE DRUM'S ENTRY at bar 17 no longer counts (0.12; v2 0.19): the bar before it is -34, not silent. THE TURN at 129 still reads under 0.10 and is 0.6 dB lower than v2's, no more: half the drum going is all that marks it. Seven sections is under the range's floor (7.7). The long loops give back more than 1: they ran out after each of the eight seeds here, but I have not shown they would under every phase of the till; feed them oftener and they may build. Which chords are heard after the first I did not measure; the third step (E minor) is outside the key. I cannot judge whether a chord at home is an arrival or another song walking in.
next: v4 on, every change behind a switch (v3 has long, turn, chord, wait on top of v2's hat, debts, till; denser stays off). (1) THE TURN (bars 129-160) is the song's idea and still its quietest: the bass could take the beats the drum gives up (the debts that fall on two and four are now free), or the till's sweep could turn with it (its phase stepped by six sixteenths). Read it on nov2.py: it wants 0.15. (2) THE DRUM'S ENTRY at bar 17: 0.12. Let the fourth seed of the opening go into the short purse so that bar 16 is bare, or bring the drum in under its own catch. Re-render seam 5 (Hearing Things into this) for the mix plan either way: the opening changed. (3) THE LONG PURSE: prove it runs out (one seed at each of the till's four quarter phases, 12 bars, level by bar); if any grows, 1.0. (4) THE CHORD: read which notes stand after one, two, three coins (lattice.py on a chord seed); if the third step's E and B natural are over -20 dB beside the seed, give home a seed every bar so the first two steps cover it. (5) THE TILL's sweep is still only shown as darker echoes: isolate one period. (6) Sections 49 and 65 (threes and fours, both purses) read nothing on the scorer: the hat's and bass's patterns change and nothing else. (7) The kick is still Least Common's. Evidence and tools: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t6-v3/ (benchg.py and benchg.sh for the purse; nov2.py; solo3.sh has the turn and home windows; facts.txt).

v4, THE PURSE INSIDE OUT (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 10:50-11:08 GMT). Not heard by me. The turn (bars 129-160, the seed off the beat) is the song's idea and was its quietest moment: under 0.10 on the scorer's curve in three versions. Three switches (--without-leave, -flip, -fill; all three off is v3 byte for byte). (1) LEAVE: the drum waits whenever the seed changes its place in the bar, to leave as well as to come home. In bars 127 and 128 drum, bass and hat stop and the three purses pay out alone (-20 and -18 dB a bar against -11 to -13). (2) FLIP: while the seed is off the beat the coins change hands (a fourth purse, d: 5 and 3). The five lifts a fifth on the left; the three drops a fourth on the right. The same amounts can be made, so hat and bass do not change; the quick coin's run now falls under the seed where it climbed over it. Read on the purse alone after the first off-beat seed (E flat 4), by sixteenths: 3, B flat 3 on the right (8 dB); 5, B flat 4 on the left (8); 6, F3 right (16); 8, F4 in the middle; 10, F5 left (15). By parts over bars 129-136 the purse is 7.4 dB under the mix (v3 8.0) and carries 24% of 120-250 Hz (15%) and 64% of 2-4 kHz (70%). (3) FILL: the break's long purse (5 and 7) gives back 1.35 a pass, not 1.05: its coins are long, so it makes fewer notes a bar and every fourth bar of the break was under -52 dB. The break by bar: -21 -23 -29 -39, -21 -23 -27 -44, -22 -23 -25 -39, -21 -24 -25 -38 (v3 -21 -27 -39 -56, -22 -26 -33 -60, -22 -27 -33 -54, -21 -28 -38 -54). PROVED that it runs out: alone after its last seed, raw by bar, -38 -44 -49 -61 -73 -81 -90 -100 -119, then nothing. At 1.5 its second bar was louder than its first, so 1.5 is too near the edge. SCORE 98.69 and 98.76 on two seeds; v3 re-read today 96.60 (seed 0). Structure 83.3 to 100: the turn now counts (0.26) and there are eight sections at every cut, inside the range (7.7 to 25.5) for the first time. Recurrence 100 to 92.3: more of the song returns, not less (four sections of six where it was three of five; the share that returns 0.68 to 0.71, and the scorer's band tops at 0.70). Only 71 Hz is more than 5 dB off the envelope (5.4 under). One build. v3's plan, 3 and 4, answered without a render: the opening's four long seeds fall at four phases of their till (0, 4, 8, 12 fifteenths) and each fell at least 16 dB in its four bars, and the till goes round inside a bar, so no seed sits at a phase that grows; the chord's third step (E and B natural) is three coins, 0.62 cubed and the loop's own 4 dB a pass, about 24 dB under the seed by arithmetic, not measured. WHAT IS WEAK: the drum's entry at bar 17 still reads 0.12. The break's fourth bars are quiet, not full: 27 to 33 dB under the groove. In level FLIP is small (the mix 1.1 dB less at 1-2 kHz, 1.7 less at 2-4): what it changes is direction and side. Its low run (B flat 3, F3, C3) is in the bass's octave. Two waits and a break are three stops in 80 bars. Sections 49 and 65 still read nothing; the drum is still Least Common's. I cannot judge whether the purse inside out reads as a turn or only as a darker echo.
next: v5 on, every change behind a switch (v4 has leave, flip, fill on top of v3's long, turn, chord, wait and v2's hat, debts, till; denser stays off). (1) BY EAR, one card: bars 125-136 of v3 beside v4, "does the purse turning inside out read as a turn". (2) RECURRENCE reads 0.71 of the song returning against a band that tops at 0.70: nothing to mend, but a section with a sound of its own (see 5) would bring it back inside. (3) THE DRUM'S ENTRY at bar 17 (0.12 since v3): the drum could come with a seed of its own bar (a seed on the one of bar 17 in the short purse, where the opening's are long) so the entry is a change of purse as well as a drum. (4) THE FLIPPED PURSE'S LOW RUN: read 120-250 Hz by bar over 129-160 beside 113-128; if the mix there is more than 2 dB up, the d loops' high-pass 150 to 220. (5) SECTIONS 49 AND 65: purse b (3 and 4) has no sound of its own; try it inside out as well (4 and 3) for its second eight bars. (6) THE CHORD: measure which notes stand after one, two, three coins (the method in facts.txt: peak of the spectrum 12 ms after each arrival). (7) The drum is still Least Common's. Both of this song's seams are as they were in v3 (bars 1-16 and the last 8 are untouched). Evidence and tools: ~/.local/state/chirper-one/clicks/t6-v4/ (benchf.py, benchf.sh and tail.sh for the purse; solo4.sh and parts.py for the turn; bars.py; nov2.py; facts.txt).

v5, SMALLER CHANGE (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 12:50-13:07 GMT). Not heard by me. One switch on (--without-smaller; off is v4 byte for byte) and one that ships off (--with-inside). SMALLER: the song ended as it began, thinner: four seeds, each with the first seed's change. Now each of the last four seeds (bars 177, 181, 185, 189) is paid in smaller coins: 3 and 5 sixteenths as ever, thirty-seconds, sixty-fourths, and then 3 and 5 of a unit that is a pitch, the period of B flat 3 (4.29 ms), in a purse with no pitch effect. Every amount from 8 units on can be made, so its change is an echo every 4.29 ms: a note. BY SOLO, the last section raw. Level by bar from each seed: sixteenths -36 -58 -83 -108; thirty-seconds -36 -68 -101 (first echoes at 193 and 317 ms, 34 peaks within 30 dB in its bar for the sixteenths' 23); sixty-fourths -35 -88 -130 (its bar by quarter -29 -40 -51 -69); the note -34 -63 -80 -97, every 250 ms -27 -33 -36 -39 -42 -45 -49 -53, and it dies. Its pitch: B flat 4 at 466.7 Hz (2 cents sharp) with F6 24 dB and B flat 6 31 dB under it; B flat 3 itself 41 under. WHAT IT TOOK: giving back 0.62 it was gone in a second, 0.66 a second and a half, 0.70 four bars (and still dies). With the other purses' high-pass at 150 Hz inside the loop the note read 13 cents sharp under in-tune harmonics (469.7 Hz): at 40 Hz, 2 cents. Taking all of the seed it stood 13 dB over the seed; at -13 dB the finished song's bar 189 read -9 dBFS; at -19 (published) -13, where the three seeds before read -17 and -18. INSIDE (off): the second purse inside out (4 and 3) in bars 57 to 64 and 73 to 80. By solo the notes at 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 sixteenths after the seed go from +6.8 -4.9 +13.9 +2.2 -9.9 semitones to -4.7 +6.8 -9.6 +2.1 +13.9, at the same level: it does what it says. With it the score is 97.52: the scorer reads 0.724 of the song as returning for 0.709 (its band stops at 0.70) and recurrence falls to 85.4. Off, and waiting for the card on the same turn at bar 129. SCORE 98.97 and 99.02 on two seeds; v4 re-read today 98.69. Recurrence 92.3 to 93.9 (share 0.712 to 0.709). FOUR BUILDS: (c) both, the note louder, 97.77 and 97.83; (d) both 97.52; (e) published. WHAT IS WEAK: the two middle steps are spent in a bar and in half a bar, so bars 183, 184 and 186 to 188 are silent (-77 to -150 in the finished song) where v4 had change in every other bar: thinning out, or holes, I cannot say. The last note's bar is still 4 to 5 dB over the other seeds'. THE SEAM with Out of Step changed: its last eight bars read -20.6 for -23.8 and hold a flurry and a held B flat, not two seeds' echoes in sixteenths (chirper-zero told; mix plan noted). The drum's entry at bar 17 is still 0.12.
next: v6 on, every change behind a switch (v5 has smaller on and inside off, on top of v4's leave, flip, fill, v3's four and v2's three; denser stays off). (1) The card q75a1507 on the turn: if the purse inside out reads as a turn, put INSIDE in (it is written and proved by solo) and read which boundary moves the scorer's returning share from 0.709 to 0.724; if "as it was" wins, FLIP and LEAVE off and INSIDE stays off. (2) BY EAR, one card when the open ones clear: the last sixteen bars of v4 beside v5 (does the change getting smaller read, is the last note an arrival, are the silences holes). (3) THE SILENCES: let the seeds come sooner as the coins get smaller (bars 177, 181, 183, 184: each wait half the last) so the song runs out as its change does and the last eight bars are the note alone; agree the seam with chirper-zero first (Out of Step's first eight bars would land on one held B flat). (4) THE NOTE PURSE AT HOME: bar 161's chord (G4 B flat 4 D5) into a purse whose unit is G3's period, so home is held where it is now struck; bench with end.sh's method (level every 250 ms, pitch, that it dies). (5) The drum's entry at bar 17 (0.12). (6) The flipped purse's low run, 120 to 250 Hz by bar over 129 to 160. (7) The drum is still Least Common's. v6, SMALL CHANGE FIRST (chirper-one, 26 Nov, 14:50-15:08 GMT). Not heard by me. The ending pays its last seeds in smaller and smaller coins, and until then nothing in the song had heard a small coin; and every new section but two simply began. Four switches (--without-roll, -gap, -lone, -tumble; all off is v5 byte for byte). (1) ROLL: on beat three of the last bar before a section, a seed on the next section's first note, paid in coins of 3 and 5 thirty-seconds where the purse stays and 3 and 5 sixty-fourths where it is new (bars 32, 48, 64, 80, 112, 144; none where the drum already waits, none before the last section). BY SOLO, raw: its seed and then 4 to 6 dB less each half beat (thirty-seconds -30 -38 -41 -45 -49, sixty-fourths -29 -35 -42 -47 -54): a flurry a beat long that runs out, not a roll that builds. (2) GAP: the drum gives beat four of that bar to the change (bars 32, 48, 64, 80, 112; at 144 it is already off four). In the finished song, beat three / beat four / the one after, v5 then v6: bar 32 -15/-15/-11 and -13/-15/-11; bar 48 -16/-16/-10 and -12/-18/-11; bar 64 -16/-16/-10 and -13/-21/-11; bar 80 -15/-16/-19 and -12/-18/-19; bar 112 -11/-13/-10 and -11/-14/-10; bar 144 -12/-15/-16 and -13/-14/-15. So beat three is up to 4 dB louder (the roll's seed on the drum) and beat four, with no drum, 0 to 5 dB under what the drum gave it. (3) LONE: the same before the drum first comes and before it comes again (bars 16 and 96), where the roll is alone. At -4 dB it read -15 dBFS on its beat where the lone seeds round it read -18 and the drum's first beat -16 (any lone sound goes to the master's ceiling): louder than everything in the opening. At -10 dB (published) it reads -18 and -24 on its two beats, then the drum at -16; at bar 96 -18 and -22, then the drum at -9. (4) TUMBLE: 'off the beat, up' (bars 145 to 160) was 'off the beat' a tone higher; now the purse turns over at every seed (inside out at 145, 149, 153, 157; the right way at 147, 151, 155, 159). By solo the echo three sixteenths after each seed is 8.0 dB to the right, then 8.0 to the left, in turn. The hat and the bass do not change (the amounts are the same). SCORE 99.62 on both seeds. HOW TO READ THAT: v5 re-read today 98.97, and the only term that moves is recurrence, on the share of the song the scorer hears as returning, whose band stops at 0.70: v5 0.709, the first build (lone rolls at -4) 0.700 and 99.95, published 0.703, the build with no lone rolls 0.715 and 98.41. Thousandths either side of an edge: the points are the scorer's, not a measure of the fills. Its eight sections are the same eight in every build; the drum's first entry at bar 17, which it read at 0.12, it now reads under 0.10. THE SEAMS: bars 13 to 16 read -20.8 for -21.5 (the flurry in bar 16, under Hearing Things' last bar); the last sixteen bars are as they were (-24.1 -23.3 -23.0 -19.2 for -24.0 -23.3 -22.9 -19.1). ALSO READ: the flipped purse's low run (planned since v4): 120 to 250 Hz stands 12.1 and 12.3 dB under the whole in the two turned sections and 11.4 to 12.5 in the others: no build-up, closed.
